resources.string: Mechanical shaft power, the nameplate value. The power drawn from the supply is higher: P / η.
Full-load power factor, from the motor nameplate.
Ratio of shaft power to input power, from the nameplate or catalogue.
Stator poles (even number): 2 poles run at about 3,000 rpm at 50 Hz, 4 poles at about 1,500 rpm.
Actual shaft speed, from the nameplate or measured with a tachometer.
Relative difference between synchronous and actual speed; 0 gives synchronous speed.
Enter the power to get the torque, or leave this blank and enter the torque.
Shaft torque. Used if the power is blank.
Optional, to get the secondary turns.
Optional, to get the primary current (ideal transformer).
In DC there is no power factor; in three-phase the voltage is line-to-line.
Calculates the current a motor draws from its shaft power, voltage, power factor and efficiency.
Calculates the mechanical power a motor delivers from the voltage and current it draws.
Calculates the supply voltage matching the motor\'s power and current.
Calculates the power factor of an AC motor from shaft power, voltage, current and efficiency.
Calculates a motor\'s efficiency by comparing shaft power with the power drawn from the supply.
Calculates the synchronous speed of an induction motor (120 × f / poles) and the rotor speed with slip.
Calculates the slip of an induction motor from its actual speed.
Relates shaft power, torque and speed: P = T × 2π × n / 60.
Calculates the turns ratio of an ideal transformer and, if given, the secondary turns and primary current.
